questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: From the numbers, how many radical chain-propagating steps are needed to convert an alkene plus HBr into an alkyl bromide with peroxide?
questions.explanation: The two propagation steps are addition of a bromine radical to the alkene to form a carbon radical, followed by abstraction of hydrogen from HBr by that carbon radical to give the alkyl bromide and regenerate a bromine radical.
questions.hint: Two propagation steps repeat.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: From the numbers, a chlorine atom radical has how many unpaired electrons?
questions.explanation: A chlorine atom has seven valence electrons and one unpaired electron, making it a radical that is eager to pair that electron by abstraction or addition.
questions.hint: One unpaired electron defines the radical.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.learningObjective: Count atoms added to the alkene
questions.stem: From the numbers, in radical addition of HBr to propene, how many new sigma bonds form at the former double bond?
questions.explanation: The pi bond is replaced by two sigma bonds, one to bromine at the terminal carbon and one to hydrogen at the internal carbon, so two new sigma bonds form across the former alkene.
questions.hint: One pi bond becomes two sigma bonds.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: From the numbers, a radical polymerization trimer contains how many monomer-derived units?
questions.explanation: A trimer by definition contains three monomer-derived units joined in a chain, each retaining the backbone atoms of the original alkene monomer.
questions.hint: Trimer means three units.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.learningObjective: Count resonance contributors of benzyl radical
questions.stem: From the numbers, how many main resonance contributors delocalize the unpaired electron of a benzyl radical into the ring?
questions.explanation: The unpaired electron of a benzyl radical is delocalized to the two ortho positions and the para position of the ring, giving three ring-centered contributors in addition to the benzylic contributor.
questions.hint: Ortho, para, and the other ortho.

questions.explanation: Peroxides contain an oxygen-oxygen bond linking two oxygen atoms, and homolysis of that weak bond under heat or light produces two alkoxy radicals that initiate chains.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Explain the following: why does the peroxide effect apply to HBr but not to HCl or HI?

answer.exemplar: The radical chain for HBr has favorable thermodynamics in both propagation steps, but for HCl the hydrogen abstraction step is too endothermic and for HI the initial iodine radical addition is endothermic, so only HBr sustains an efficient radical chain and shows anti-Markovnikov addition.

questions.explanation: Both propagation steps must be favorable. The radical chain for HBr has favorable thermodynamics in both propagation steps, but for HCl the hydrogen abstraction step is too endothermic and for HI the initial iodine radical addition is endothermic, so only HBr sustains an efficient radical chain and shows anti-Markovnikov addition.
questions.hint: Bond strengths differ down the halogen series.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Explain the following: why are allylic radicals more stable than simple alkyl radicals?

answer.exemplar: The unpaired electron of an allylic radical is delocalized over three adjacent carbons through resonance, with contributors placing the radical at either end of the allyl system; this spreading of the unpaired electron lowers the energy compared with a localized alkyl radical.

questions.explanation: Resonance delocalizes the unpaired electron. The unpaired electron of an allylic radical is delocalized over three adjacent carbons through resonance, with contributors placing the radical at either end of the allyl system; this spreading of the unpaired electron lowers the energy compared with a localized alkyl radical.
questions.hint: Two terminal sites share the radical.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Explain the following: why can a single initiator radical lead to many product molecules?

answer.exemplar: Each propagation step consumes one radical but generates another, so the radical center is passed along and the sequence repeats many times before two radicals finally combine in termination; this chain process amplifies one initiation event into a large number of product molecules.

questions.explanation: Radicals are regenerated in propagation. Each propagation step consumes one radical but generates another, so the radical center is passed along and the sequence repeats many times before two radicals finally combine in termination; this chain process amplifies one initiation event into a large number of product molecules.
questions.hint: Termination eventually stops the chain.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Explain the following: why does NBS give allylic bromination instead of addition to the double bond?

answer.exemplar: NBS maintains a very low concentration of bromine, which suppresses electrophilic addition across the alkene, while radical abstraction of a weak allylic C-H bond is fast; the resulting resonance-stabilized allylic radical then reacts with bromine to give the allylic bromide.

questions.explanation: Low bromine concentration avoids addition. NBS maintains a very low concentration of bromine, which suppresses electrophilic addition across the alkene, while radical abstraction of a weak allylic C-H bond is fast; the resulting resonance-stabilized allylic radical then reacts with bromine to give the allylic bromide.
questions.hint: Weak allylic C-H bonds are abstracted.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Provide the explanation: why does the peroxide effect apply to HBr but not to HCl or HI?

answer.exemplar: The radical chain for HBr has favorable thermodynamics in both propagation steps, but for HCl the hydrogen abstraction step is too endothermic and for HI the initial iodine radical addition is endothermic, so only HBr sustains an efficient radical chain and shows anti-Markovnikov addition.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Provide the explanation: why are allylic radicals more stable than simple alkyl radicals?

answer.exemplar: The unpaired electron of an allylic radical is delocalized over three adjacent carbons through resonance, with contributors placing the radical at either end of the allyl system; this spreading of the unpaired electron lowers the energy compared with a localized alkyl radical.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Provide the explanation: why can a single initiator radical lead to many product molecules?

answer.exemplar: Each propagation step consumes one radical but generates another, so the radical center is passed along and the sequence repeats many times before two radicals finally combine in termination; this chain process amplifies one initiation event into a large number of product molecules.
